columns: Checked against your part before printing

rows.name: AI image-to-3D
rows.why: It infers a shape from a picture, so sizes are a guess, and you get a mesh to work with.

rows.name: Phone scan apps
rows.why: A scan needs many photos of the part, and small plastic parts tend to come out rough.

rows.name: Text-to-CAD
rows.why: You get editable CAD, but you supply the sizes, and nothing compares the result with your part.

rows.name: Part libraries
rows.why: These work well when someone already modelled your exact part. If nobody did, there is nothing to find.

rows.name: CAD by hand
rows.why: It is accurate in skilled hands, but it takes a caliper and CAD skills, and the first real check is often a test print.

rows.name: PartSmith
rows.why: Screen markers set the scale, code measures, an agent writes the program, and the verifier compares it with the photo before export.

landscape.finding: We found none that check the result against your part, in millimetres, before you print.
